# URGENT — implementation must match the model (paper/model.tex) — 2026-09-07
<!-- Generated by Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic); decisions by Fatih -->
Reference audit: notes/model_tex_vs_implementation_audit.md. The model text is the specification; the
items below are the code changes needed so that the extractor produces exactly what the paper defines.

## 1. dep edges — WRONG aspect attribution (big one)
Model: a service call yields a request edge from the calling callback f to the serving callback g and a
response edge from g to f's continuation. Nothing else.
Code (model_improved_pg.py): identify_entities gives every `cli` entity aspects [(pub, service),
(sub, service)], the same shape as a server; add_horizontal_edges builds srv_index from every (sub, service)
aspect, so client entities are treated as servers and receive request edges from the requesting callback's
entity (which carries the `cli` aspect from fish_rclcpp_client_link). Evidence (fish_20260906_151532):
request tmr→cli 11, serv→cli 8 vs tmr→serv 5, serv→serv 6 — 19 of 30 request edges end at a client
entity of the same node. Every service chain therefore has a spurious parallel path
requester → client-entity → continuation.
Fix: (a) client entities get NO (sub, service)/(pub, service) aspects (their F is the execute_client
dispatch = the response handler); (b) srv_index only from etype == "serv"; (c) response edge target = the
requester's continuation F (split_callbacks), with the client entity's F kept as the dispatch vertex on
that response path if we want the execute_client span visible — decide one representation and make the
L2/L3 propagation follow it. Re-extract the paper sessions afterwards.

## 2. Edge lifting for every type
Model: a vertex inherits every edge between its children and another vertex's children, whatever the
type; higher-layer edges are sets of callback-layer edge tuples.
Code: L1/L0 are aggregated from L2 msg/dep only; join/state/polled exist only at L3; gxf never leaves L2.
Fix: aggregate from L3 upward for all natures (keep counts per type in the edge attrs), drop the
L2-based aggregation.

## 3. Out-of-ROS threads as external vertices
Model: a thread outside the launch tree exchanging data over topics is flagged oort at the callback
layer; its edges are external; lifted, it becomes an external entity of that layer.
Code: detect_oort_threads creates an `oore` entity + `oort` F inside the process's FIRST node, edges not
flagged; oort F have no phase (runs after mark_phases). Fix: external-flagged edges, external entity on
lift, phase assignment, no arbitrary node parent (attach to the process / external vertex).

## 4. Polled edges as a type
Model: `polled` is an edge type (observed sample-and-hold read); `state` is the inferred one.
Code: nature=state with polled=true/inferred=false. Fix: nature=polled.

## 5. Callback-layer GPU DAG attachment
Model: edges into a GPU-submitting callback attach to the entry of its typed DAG, outgoing edges leave
from its exit. Code: gpu_dags are stored per anchor, not wired into graph_edges. Fix: expose entry/exit
nodes and connect them (at least in the export/viz).

## 6. Task route (deferred; tasks are out of the WiP text)
_serve_task_graphs decomposes over all comm edges; wcc_dag_viz --data-only implements the data-edge rule.

## Unchanged by decision (paper abstraction wins): attribute field names (mode, hostname, phase set),
namespace grouping wording, memset engine typing, aspect fallback.

## 7. `gpu_node` is per-process, not per-callback (found while drawing the model figure)
identify_callbacks sets `gpu_node=True` on EVERY F of a process that has a CUDA context, so in Autoware all
~500 callbacks of `pointcloud_container` are flagged. The model's "a callback that submits GPU work" is the
typed-DAG anchor set (gpu_dags, anchor_type='cb') — 6 callbacks in fish_20260906_151532. The figure generator
(postprocess/paper_fig_model.py) marks submitters from gpu_dags, not from the flag. Fix: rename the attribute
to `gpu_process` and add `gpu_submitter` from the typed-DAG anchors.
